full_judgment:
21. By drawing our attention the decision in the case of the Government of Bangladesh Appellant Vs.  Asraf Ali and another Respondents reported in 2 MLR (AD)96, Mr. Rokon Uddin Mahmud next submits that the enlistment of the case property as an abandoned property in the 'Ka' list has a presumptive value in la as to its correctness unless it is rebutted by adducing evidence to the contrary; but it transpires that the petitioner has failed to rebut the presumption of correctness attached to the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings by adducing evidence to the contrary and this being the scenario, the judgment and order of the lower Court is not liable to be interfered with. 

 "8. It has been held by this Division in various decisions that the enlistment of a building under Section 5(1) of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 raises a presumption in law that the property is an abandoned property under Section 5(2) of the Ordinance. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable presumption; but the respondent No. 1 failed to rebut this presumption. No rebuttable evidence could be adduced to show that the original owner Yahiya was present in Bangladesh and he occupied, managed or supervised the disputed building when the P.O. No. 16 of 1972 came into operation. Hence the listing of the property as an abandoned property in the Supplementary. Provisions Ordinance, 1985 was lawful as it was an abandoned property by operation of law".
